stories.headline: Madhur Bhandarkar renames 'The Wives' to 'The Wives Of Bollywood' after audience confusion
stories.what: Filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar has renamed his upcoming film from 'The Wives' to 'The Wives Of Bollywood', citing audience confusion about the subject of the film. Bhandarkar revealed that people were asking whether the title referred to a show about co-wives or a general concept, prompting the clarification through a more specific title. The rename signals the importance of brand clarity for a filmmaker who has built his career on behind-the-scenes Bollywood exposés.
stories.lens: For a film that will inevitably be compared to Bhandarkar's earlier industry dramas like Fashion and Page 3, the clearer title directly positions the film for its intended audience.
stories.article:
Madhur Bhandarkar has decided to rename his upcoming project from the simply titled 'The Wives' to 'The Wives Of Bollywood', after feedback indicated that audiences were confused about what — or who — the film was actually about. The director confirmed the change to The Times of India, explaining that viewers were asking whether the title referred to co-wives.

The confusion is understandable: 'The Wives' as a standalone title offers little context, whereas 'The Wives Of Bollywood' immediately communicates the film's world and likely subject matter. For Bhandarkar, who made his name with films that peeled back the glamour of the entertainment industry, the Bollywood setting is a familiar and commercially reliable backdrop.

The rename is a pragmatic piece of audience management — in an era of streaming and social media, a film's title is often its first piece of marketing. A title that requires explanation is a title that risks losing casual interest before a single frame is shown.

Bhandarkar's track record with industry-set films, including the acclaimed Fashion and Page 3, means audience expectations for 'The Wives Of Bollywood' will be high. The title change, minor as it appears, suggests the director is focused on ensuring the film reaches its intended audience with maximum clarity.
key_facts: Film renamed from 'The Wives' to 'The Wives Of Bollywood'
Director Madhur Bhandarkar cited audience confusion
Audiences reportedly asked if it was about co-wives

stories.headline: Saif Ali Khan calls for Bollywood bravery after 'Dhurandhar' crosses Rs 3100 crore
stories.what: Actor Saif Ali Khan has made a pointed call for Bollywood to 'be brave' in the wake of Dhurandhar becoming a massive box-office success, crossing Rs 3100 crore. The statement signals a growing conversation in the industry about the kind of content Hindi cinema needs to produce to compete with regional and global fare. Saif's remarks come at a time when Bollywood is under sustained pressure to rediscover its commercial footing after a string of high-profile underperformers.
stories.lens: With Dhurandhar clearing Rs 3100 crore, Saif's call for creative risk-taking could shape how Bollywood's producers and studios green-light projects in the coming year.
stories.article:
Dhurandhar's staggering Rs 3100 crore box-office run has given Saif Ali Khan a platform to push for a fundamental shift in how Bollywood approaches storytelling. In a candid conversation with The Indian Express, the actor argued that Hindi cinema 'needs to be brave' — a message that lands with particular weight given the film's blockbuster performance.

The success of Dhurandhar comes amid a broader reckoning for Bollywood, where audiences have been consistently gravitating towards bolder regional productions and big-ticket franchise films. Saif's remarks suggest that the formula for revival is not just bigger budgets but more daring creative choices.

For an industry that has spent recent years reassessing its relationship with audiences, the timing of these comments is significant. The film's commercial triumph provides concrete evidence that Indian viewers are willing to show up in massive numbers for the right kind of content.

Whether Saif's call to arms translates into a production culture shift remains to be seen, but the Rs 3100 crore benchmark now serves as both inspiration and challenge for the studios and filmmakers who will greenlight the next wave of Hindi films.

Saif Ali Khan says Bollywood 'needs to be brave'
